subject.title: fix(browser): stop screenshot vision-failure fallback from injecting raw base64

question: Should configured browser-vision failures return the PR's text-only failure/share result, or should OpenClaw retain a session-safe model-visible screenshot recovery path for transient provider failures?
rationale: Both choices avoid the reported base64 persistence problem, but they make different user-facing recovery guarantees that tests cannot select on behalf of browser owners.

options.title: Approve text-only recovery
options.body: Adopt the branch behavior: report the vision failure as text and retain only the staged outbound file path for explicit sharing.

options.title: Design safe image recovery
options.body: Keep a model-visible recovery path only if it is carried outside retained tool-result/session context and receives focused upgrade and session-state proof.

options.title: Pause pending owner direction
options.body: Leave the PR open without merging until a browser-area owner chooses the intended configured-vision failure contract.

recommendation.title: Approve text-only recovery
recommendation.body: Adopt the branch behavior: report the vision failure as text and retain only the staged outbound file path for explicit sharing.

likelyOwner.reason: The available material identifies the browser-plugin decision boundary but not an evidence-backed individual owner.
